notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 388,100 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 45% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 38% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 18% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the building clears every hard mandate filter but misses the yield-on-cost, unlevered IRR and equity multiple targets at the asking price.

Buy at AED 64.2m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 24% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]]. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the exit yield, at 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either side, which swings the price by AED 10.7m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and returns rest on the firm's house view of rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime, not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Cedarline Residences, Dubai Silicon Oasis, 112 units [[om.unit_count]], completed in 2013 [[deal.completion_year]]. Freehold, single title.
- **Price:** asking AED 84.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], AED 796 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA, or AED 589 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] on BUA.
- **Income:** in-place rent AED 7.9m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] from direct leases, with no master tenant. Occupancy is 95% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units and 94% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area. The landlord pays chiller costs.

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | 4.2% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple | 1.20x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.9% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 6.3% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |

Year-1 NOI is AED 5.3m [[uw.noi_year1]]. The yield miss is small; the IRR miss is large.

Levered, secondary: IRR 2.6% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]], equity multiple 1.13x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]], Year-1 DSCR 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM headline yield is 6.0% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 5.9% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The OM's figure holds up on its own basis, but the buyer's figure is just under the mandate minimum.

## What would make it fail
- **Exit yield.** With the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is 3.1% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. The base case already has a gross exit value of AED 82.4m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], below the purchase price.
- **Rent and exit together.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is 1.4% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. Levered IRR is then a loss of 1.9% a year [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **No grid case reaches target.** The best case has market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter. Unlevered IRR is 7.0% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], still under the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target.
- **Expiry cluster.** 35% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent, AED 2.8m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]], expires between 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 29 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. That is inside the mandate limit, but it falls in the year when the house view has market rents falling 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]].

## Discrepancies
The facts list no material discrepancies between the documents and the screen. The OM's occupancy, rent and yield tie to the rent roll and operating statement. The screen's Year-1 NOI is slightly above the statement NOI because it models leases one by one, net of downtime, and then deducts vacancy, fees and VAT. Nothing lower-severity is discussed because nothing was flagged.

## Checks before diligence
- Deposits of AED 388,100 [[notice.security_deposits]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Cheque profile: 18% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on the longest cheque schedules, and more cheques mean more collection risk. Check the post-dated cheque cover.
- Test the OM's reversion claim against the rent roll, including the notice timing. The facts show no over-rented units.
- Confirm the status of the units under renewal and those with notice served.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold, single title, buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.

## Assumptions
House view: exit yield of 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]], which includes 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. Market rents fall 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then rise 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The loan is AED 35.0m [[uw.loan_aed]], 41% [[uw.ltv]] LTV against a 45% [[assume.max_ltv]] cap. It is sized to a 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR at a 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] rate, with 15 years [[assume.amortisation_years]] of amortisation. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. No operating cost lines were filled from mandate defaults.
